design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing only: that the form she posted to leave the plan be acted on. Nothing she says names a figure, a charge, a subsidy or a second piece of work. A correct agent reads the published rule for ending an enrollment, finds in it the sentence "The closing premium balance is not struck before the premium relief the member is owed stands on the premium account as a credit entry", looks at the premium account, sees that no such entry stands there, works out from the other published rule which write puts one there, computes it from a ledger and from the low income premium subsidy recorded on the drug plan the member held before this one, posts it, and only then strikes the closing balance on the world that write has changed. The difficulty is entirely in reading policy, reconciling history and arithmetic; there is no tool to guess at, nothing the customer must be asked that she cannot answer, and she never corrects a wrong path.

ROUND 2 — WHAT THE SOURCE AUDIT FOUND AND WHAT WAS DONE. This task was rebuilt against `audits/policy_task/medicare_advantage_member_services/_difficulty.md` and `0.md`. Item by item:

F3 / 0-R1 (the undefined term "relief credit" gave the scored credit_amount two defensible values, 370.95 and 517.95). Closed by naming in the rule exactly what the compute counts. Every place the charter said "relief credit" as a selector now says "credit adjustment", with the qualifier "whatever reason each of them carries" carried in the tier itself: "the relief already set off is every credit adjustment posted on the account in the contract year, whatever reason each of them carries". The binding is unchanged — `COUNT/SUM('advantage_premium_ledger', event_type='advantage_premium_credit_adjustment')` — and the prose now says precisely that, so the narrow reading the audit constructed is no longer available. The same wording was applied to the closing-balance policy and to the reinstatement policy, which shared the term.

F4 (the prose "both months included" against a whole-month `MONTHS(...)+1`). Closed by describing the expression exactly instead of a calendar span: "The coverage months reckoned as owed are the whole months that have passed since the coverage effective date, and one more for the month in hand." That sentence is a literal reading of `MONTHS(d1, NOW) + 1` for every pair of dates, so prose and expression can no longer diverge. The same replacement was made in the closing-balance policy and in the reinstatement policy.

F5 / 0-R2 (the root computation carried no honest `parameter` factor: both ladders labelled parameter selected rows or formulas). Closed by rebuilding the closing-balance policy's ladders rather than relabelling them. It now carries two ladders that select a published number — `final_period_months`, which selects among the policy's own month counts (three coverage months, one, or none), each of them a coverage month the enrollment has already been in force for, and `unbilled_month_share`, which selects among the policy's own subsidy shares (none, a quarter, half, three quarters or the whole) — and three that select rows or formulas and are labelled `method`: `settlement_charge_reckoning`, `settlement_payment_selection`, `settlement_relief_allowance`. The relief-credit policy's labels were honest already (`member_premium_share` and `subsidy_award_reachback` select K figures) and are unchanged.

0-R3 (a Part D low-income subsidy halving the premium of the one tier that carries no Part D). Closed by reseeding rather than rewording. The member now holds Ridgecrest Advantage Premier (PPO), whose `part_d_included` is true, so the low income premium subsidy reduces a plan premium that genuinely includes prescription drug coverage — which is exactly what base `advantage_premium_billing` provides for ("Where the member qualifies for the low-income premium subsidy the full premium is still charged and the subsidy is posted separately as a credit adjustment"). Her stand-alone Ridgecrest RxSecure Select drug plan is now the plan she held before this one: it stands `disenrolled` with `coverage_end_date 2025-12-31`, the day before the Medicare Advantage coverage began, with `disenrollment_reason_code enrolled_in_ma_pd` — the ending base `advantage_drug_coverage_exclusivity` requires when an elected tier includes Part D. The CMS award and the subsidy credits the plan posted while that drug plan was in force sit on its record, which is where a sponsor reads its own record of a member's award. The reachback ladder was re-keyed off a three-month window onto the credits standing on that account, so it reads an ended account correctly.

0-O1 (one persona line pointed at the answer's neighbourhood). The reactive line now reads "If the representative says there is something they must put right on her record before they can settle with her" — no longer naming the premium account.

0-O2 (the whole-baseline fall-back of the relief computation is 0.00, so a baseline-only reader concludes no relief is owed). Still 0.00 on this world and recorded as accepted: the baseline reading charges the member the whole 47.60 for nine coverage months, 428.40, against 180.00 reckoned on the account, so the policy's own trigger does not fire and the fall-back answer is "nothing to post". That is a definite, wrong, business-shaped conclusion rather than an error, and it is the fall-back the computation document alone produces.

0-O3 (a seeded account no compliant billing run produces). Kept and made explicit in `seed_consistency`: the two quarterly charges of 180.00 were raised at a superseded monthly rate of 60.00 rather than the tier's 47.60. The charter contemplates exactly this (the account already carries a `billing_error_correction` credit and the enum provides for it), and the over-billing is what the relief addresses.

SCOPE, AND WHAT TASK 1 CLAIMS. Task 0 claims `advantage_ext_premium_subsidy_relief` (subject advantage_premium_credit_adjustment, tool post_premium_relief_credit_3acf64b3) and `advantage_ext_disenrollment_closing_balance` (subject advantage_voluntary_disenrollment, tool end_plan_membership_007ca425). Task 1 claims the other three. No subject event, target tool or computed quantity is shared. The two scopes are pairwise disjoint and jointly cover all five extended policies.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. `draw_counts.py … --task 0` prints {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. The tree has one prerequisite problem and each computation carries five declared factors.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: `advantage_ext_disenrollment_closing_balance`, the problem the customer's surface request points at. Prerequisite: `advantage_ext_premium_subsidy_relief`. One edge, kind value_input, gate `relief_allowed` (a real compute binding of the blocked policy, renamed this round from `credits_allowed` when the policy was rebuilt), form state, so no fallback_reason. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root's own rule: "The closing premium balance is not struck before the premium relief the member is owed stands on the premium account as a credit entry." Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result to what it waits on with the connective "before", in the negated direction — the direction a settlements desk uses for a balance it will not strike yet; rewritten affirmatively it reads "the closing premium balance is struck only once the premium relief the member is owed stands on the premium account as a credit entry", the exact contrapositive, same result, same waited-on state, same scope; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state, a credit entry standing on the premium account, in the words the premium ledger and its finder use, with no action, performer or tool; (3) no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id; (4) exactly the strength of the edge. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only `post_premium_relief_credit_3acf64b3` creates an `advantage_premium_credit_adjustment` row. Derivation: the sentence names a premium relief credit standing on the account; the account read at action 3 carries only a billing error correction of 60.00; the other published rule says what the premium relief credited to a member is and that it is posted as a credit entry on that account; therefore it must be computed and posted first. Resolved by that tool, owner agent; the customer's own write is the root's own action, `end_plan_membership_007ca425`, owner user. Seed evidence that the edge is false at the opening: `initial_state.advantage_premium_ledger.9174caeb-e2ff-4ef7-b174-66051d89e8d5.adjustment_reason_code = billing_error_correction` at `.amount = 60.00`, the two charges at 180.00 each, and `initial_state.pdp_enrollments.5605f889-e538-4ef3-8752-c403f60c45fe.low_income_subsidy_applied = partial_subsidy_50`, the award that makes relief owed and has left no trace on this account. Topological order: relief, then closing balance — a single chain, so no parallel edges to reorder, and base entails the same order independently, since `advantage_premium_posting` allows a credit adjustment only while the enrollment is active, premium_grace_period or terminated_for_nonpayment, and the member's own write leaves it disenrolled. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping the relief leaves one credit adjustment standing and none of it inside three months, so the relief allowed falls from 288.60 to 0.00 and the closing balance comes out 391.40 instead of 102.80. The tool layer blocks nothing: see `prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block`.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Write 1, subject advantage_premium_credit_adjustment. The only governing base policy is `advantage_premium_posting`; the only gate applying to a credit adjustment is `account_open_for_posting` ("The enrollment is in a status of active, premium_grace_period or terminated_for_nonpayment on the day the money is posted"), authority system_record, correlation advantage_enrollments.advantage_enrollment_id bound to the action argument of the same name. The enrollment is active, so it holds; had it been disenrolled it would not, which is also why the order cannot be reversed. One clause of that base policy is superseded, and declared: "may never exceed the amount of that charge; a credit larger than one charge is split across the charges it relieves", replaced by the single-entry sentence in the extended rule. That override is exercised on this world — the relief of 228.60 exceeds the 180.00 charge it names, and the tool records the balance effect as an overpayment. Every other clause of that base policy stays in force and is respected: the credit names the single charge it relieves and the reason it was granted, money is posted oldest unpaid month first, nothing is credited until it is on the plan's record. Write 2, subject advantage_voluntary_disenrollment. The only governing base policy is `advantage_disenrollment_and_withdrawal`, gate `member_request_recorded`; the intake carries request_action voluntary_disenrollment and intake_status recorded, so it holds. Its authorisation sentence, the last-day-of-month effective rule and the Original-Medicare warning are carried into the extended rule; nothing of it is overridden. No time gate applies to either write, so `temporal_feasibility` is empty.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Write 1's object is the single plan premium charge the credit names, the entry posted 2026-04-01 for coverage month 2026-04 at 180.00, which is the most recent plan premium charge standing on the account; the tool writes that reference into `source_premium_entry_id`, so the credit carries a unique link to its source object. Write 2's object is the enrollment together with the member's own intake. Rows included in every aggregate: the five entries carrying this enrollment's reference, all of them returned by the premium-ledger read at action 3. The member's ended drug plan account is a different table reached by a different read at action 6, and its four rows are not all excluded: three of them, the low income premium subsidy credits of 2025-10-05, 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05, are exactly what the reachback ladder counts and are worth 71.40 of the scored relief. The one row that is excluded is the drug plan's own premium charge of 34.80, which a careless reader counts as a fourth subsidy credit; the ladder excludes it by naming the reason a credit must carry, and counting it would give four where the rule gives three.

FACTOR CARD — advantage_ext_premium_subsidy_relief (5 factors: 2 parameter, 3 method; 2 cross-difficulty on pdp; 2 multi-source). owed_month_count, method, decides owed_months; tier taken: quarterly with two charges against nine coverage months in force, so three months per charge, 6; baseline the whole months passed since the effective date and one more, 9; result under it 157.20. member_premium_share, parameter, cross-difficulty on pdp, decides member_share; evidence `initial_state.pdp_enrollments.5605f889-e538-4ef3-8752-c403f60c45fe.low_income_subsidy_applied = partial_subsidy_50`; tier taken: half, so a coverage month costs 23.80; baseline the whole, 47.60; result under it 157.20. subsidy_award_reachback, parameter, cross-difficulty on pdp, decides reachback_months; evidence the three low income premium subsidy credits of 17.40 standing on that drug plan account; tier taken: three coverage months; baseline none; result under it 157.20. premium_reckoned_selection, method, decides charges_reckoned; tier taken: every charge of the contract year, 360.00; baseline the most recent charge, 180.00; result under it 48.60. relief_set_off_selection, method, decides relief_set_off; tier taken: every credit adjustment of the contract year whatever reason it carries, 60.00; baseline nothing; result under it 288.60. Whole baseline 0.00 against gold 228.60. Near-miss: the drug plan's own premium charge of 34.80, which a careless reader counts as a subsidy credit, excluded by the reason the ladder names.

FACTOR CARD — advantage_ext_disenrollment_closing_balance (5 factors: 2 parameter, 3 method; 1 cross-difficulty on pdp; 2 multi-source). settlement_charge_reckoning, method, decides charges_reckoned; tier taken: every charge of the contract year, 360.00; baseline the most recent charge, 180.00; result under it 0.00. final_period_months, parameter, decides final_months; tier taken: quarterly with the charges leaving three of the nine coverage months in force uncovered, so three coverage months; baseline none; result under it 31.40. unbilled_month_share, parameter, cross-difficulty on pdp, decides unbilled_share; tier taken: half, so such a coverage month is charged at 23.80; baseline the whole, 47.60; result under it 174.20. settlement_payment_selection, method, decides payments_allowed; tier taken: every payment of the contract year, 40.00; baseline the most recent payment, 20.00; result under it 122.80. settlement_relief_allowance, method, decides relief_allowed; tier taken: every credit adjustment of the contract year whatever reason each carries, 288.60; baseline nothing; result under it 391.40. Whole baseline 160.00 against gold 102.80.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The Premier tier supplies the monthly plan premium of 47.60 and the quarterly cadence four ladders test, and it carries prescription drug coverage, which is what makes the subsidy story honest. The two quarterly charges at 180.00 are the superseded 60.00 monthly rate carried into the contract year: they are the over-billing the relief addresses and they put the customer off the fall-through of both charge-reckoning ladders. The two part payments of 20.00 make the payment ladders bite; a single payment would put her on their fall-through. The May credit adjustment of 60.00 makes both relief ladders bite and is the credit that is not the relief owed, which is what keeps the prerequisite genuinely unmet. The ended drug plan supplies the CMS award and, through the three subsidy credits standing on its account, the reachback evidence; its own premium charge is the near-miss beside them. The intake is the member's own recorded request, without which the enrollment could not be ended. The enrollment's `premium_balance_due` of 320.00 is a deliberately stale cache — the charges of 360.00 less the payments of 40.00, as the account stood before the credit of 60.00 was posted — and no rule of either policy reads it, so an agent who reads the field instead of reconciling the ledger gets a wrong number with no signal. `moop_accumulated` is 0.00 and no rule of this task reads it. Base's automatic clauses were checked row by row: the first unpaid charge was posted 2026-01-02 and this tier's grace period is 90 days, but the plan has not put the enrollment into the grace period and no delinquency write is owed by this task set; no claim or coverage request is seeded, so neither the cost-share nor the timeliness policy can ignite an obligation.

PERSONA DESIGN. Marjorie is unhurried and slightly anxious, packing to move, with one administrative worry. Volunteered at the opening: that she posted the form, that she is moving to her daughter, that she authorises the representative and will do in person anything reserved to her. Given only when asked: her telephone number, the Medicare identifier, the ZIP code, her date of birth, that nobody acts for her, and what she means to do for cover after leaving. Reacted to only after the representative speaks: the go-ahead when told something must be put right on her record, the carrying out of the handed-over step, and the close once she hears the membership has ended and what day coverage runs to. She cannot say what she has paid and refers the representative to the record. Her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Actions 0 and 1 find and verify her; action 2 gives the tier, the frequency and the effective date; action 3 gives every premium entry on the account; action 4 gives the recorded request; actions 5 and 6 give the drug plan record and its subsidy credits; actions 7 and 8 post the relief; actions 9 and 10 hand her own write over and she runs it. All under the single frozen_time 2026-09-21 10:20:00 PDT. Nothing waits on a diagnosis, a delivery, a clearing, a review or a future date.

WHAT IS EASILY GOT WRONG. Folding the drug plan's four ledger rows into the Medicare Advantage aggregates (excluded because every binding is scoped to the holding being settled). Counting the drug plan's premium charge as a subsidy credit (excluded by the reason the ladder names). Striking the closing balance before posting the relief (excluded by the prerequisite sentence, and by base's posting gate). Pricing the coverage months the settlement still charges for at the whole 47.60 rather than the member's half (excluded by the subsidy the drug plan record carries). Reading `premium_balance_due` off the enrollment instead of reconciling the ledger (excluded because no rule reads it).

STANDARD SOLUTION. Read the enrollment, the whole premium account, the intake, the drug plan and its ledger. Relief: 360.00 reckoned, 6 coverage months owed less 3 reached back over, 3 chargeable at 23.80 each, less 60.00 already set off, gives 228.60, posted against the 2026-04-01 charge with the low income premium subsidy reason. Closing balance on the world that write leaves: 360.00 reckoned, plus the three uncovered coverage months at 23.80, less 40.00 of payments, less 288.60 of credit adjustments, gives 102.80. Hand the ending over and let her run it with that figure.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. Both computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator at each write's handling time before any gold was filled in. Output: relief 228.6, touched 3, per-factor baselines 157.2, 157.2, 157.2, 48.6, 288.6, all-baseline 0; closing balance 102.8, touched 6, per-factor baselines 0, 31.4, 174.2, 122.8, 391.4, all-baseline 160.0; closing balance with the prerequisite skipped 391.4. Those are exactly the figures the computations carry. The published gates then confirmed it: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (11 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, no errors, closure 13 of 13 rows); check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK (2 calls, 2 base gates, 6 seed rows); check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK; check_grounding --task 0 GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire --task 0 SCOPE OK.

REVISION LOG. Round 1: the premium ledger was read by enrollment reference, so rows on a second enrollment never entered the closure; action 3 now reads by member reference. Round 2, against the source audit: F3 closed by naming the credit adjustments the compute counts; F4 closed by describing the month count exactly; F5 and 0-R2 closed by rebuilding the closing-balance ladders so two of them select published numbers; 0-R3 closed by moving the member to an MA-PD tier and making the stand-alone drug plan the one she held before it; 0-O1 closed in the persona. Every downstream reference was propagated in the same pass: the charter's five policies, the seed, both computations and all ten factor sensitivities, the two gold arguments, the prerequisite gate name and its figures, `seed_consistency`, `required_user_inputs`, the argument tracing and this dossier. Re-run result: all seven gates green.

RULE AND COMPUTE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Forward, every binding of both policies that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim compute_basis quotation, checked by script to be a whitespace-insensitive substring of its own policy's rule. Backward, each load-bearing sentence was walked to its binding: the month-counting sentences to `MONTHS(...) + 1`, now worded as the expression computes; each ladder paragraph to its ternary chain; "rounded to the nearest cent once at the end" to the single RND wrapping each result, the only intermediate roundings being the ones the rules state for the plan premium of a coverage month; "never less than nothing" to the MX(0, ...) guards; the subtraction order written out in the result sentence. Every event_type and window filter in an expression has its sentence, and no sentence is unclaimed.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and what the customer says: she wants her membership ended; the published rule says the closing balance is not struck before the premium relief she is owed stands on the account as a credit entry, and the account shows only a May billing error correction; the published relief rule gives, on these records, 360.00 less 3 coverage months at 23.80 less 60.00, that is 228.60, posted against the most recent charge with the low income premium subsidy reason; the closing balance rule then gives 360.00 plus 71.40 less 40.00 less 288.60, that is 102.80. The draft agrees with gold in the object handled, the order of the two writes and both figures, and no second equally grounded reading survives: the credit-adjustment selector is now named by the rule, and the month count is described exactly as it is computed.

ROUND 3 — WHAT THE SECOND SOURCE AUDIT FOUND AND WHAT WAS DONE. Three of the five new defects bear on this task.

N1 and N2 (the seventy-five-per-cent subsidy tier bound 0.75 where its own rule sentence says a quarter, and the enum value partial_subsidy_25 was swept into the no-subsidy fall-through). Closed, and swept through every face rather than only the one the audit quoted. Both subsidy ladders this task uses — `member_premium_share` on the relief and `unbilled_month_share` on the closing balance — now carry five tiers, one for each state the drug-plan record can be in: a full subsidy leaves the member meeting none of the monthly plan premium, a seventy-five per cent subsidy a quarter, a fifty per cent subsidy half, a twenty-five per cent subsidy three quarters, and no subsidy the whole. The parameter keys were corrected with them — `quarter_member_share` is 0.25 and `three_quarter_member_share` is 0.75, each bound to the tier its own sentence names — and the rule paragraph, the compute expression, the `compute_basis` quotation, the ladder and this dossier were all changed in the same pass. No scored value moves: this member's record shows `partial_subsidy_50`, so she meets half either way, and the relief is still 228.60 and the closing balance still 102.80.

N3 (the `final_period_months` tier charged 'the three coverage months of the quarter in hand', which for a member leaving early in an unbilled quarter would charge coverage months beginning after the coverage end date, against base's sentence forbidding exactly that). Closed by routing the rule around the base clause rather than overriding it, because base is right: a plan does not charge for a coverage month that begins after coverage ends. The tier now keys on how many coverage months the enrollment has already been in force for that the charges leave uncovered — at least three gives three, fewer than three gives one, none gives none — so the months charged are always months already served, and the rule now says so outright: 'No coverage month beginning after the coverage end date is ever charged into the closing settlement, because the coverage months the settlement still charges for are only ever coverage months the enrollment has already been in force for.' `overwrite` stays `[]` because nothing of base is superseded. On this world the figure is unchanged at three coverage months, since the charges cover January to June and the enrollment has been in force January to September.

2-R3 (the object-and-rows paragraph asserted that four drug-plan rows were excluded and visible in the same call, when three of them are counted by the reachback ladder and all four are reached by a different finder on a different table). Closed by rewriting that paragraph to say what the recomputation shows: the five premium entries are the aggregated rows, the drug plan's four rows come from the read at action 6, three of them are counted and worth 71.40 of the relief, and the one genuinely excluded row is the 34.80 premium charge. The sentence three paragraphs later that already said this is now consistent with it.

2-O1 (the reseed removed this task's only discriminating near-miss, and the 34.80 drug-plan charge does not move a tier because counting it gives four against a threshold of at least three). Accepted as an observation and recorded rather than papered over: the excluded record is real and is excluded by the rule alone, but a reader who miscounts it lands on the same tier, so it tests the reading of the reason filter rather than the tier boundary. Computation B's discriminating records are the two payments and the two credit adjustments, each of which moves its own ladder off the fall-through.

Re-run after these changes: check_extended EXTENDED OK, check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, replay_tasks REPLAY OK, check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK, check_compute COMPUTE OK, check_grounding GROUNDING OK, check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

ROUND 4 — WHAT THE THIRD SOURCE AUDIT FOUND AND WHAT WAS DONE. One item bears on this task.

3-R1 (two proof fields still grounded the `final_period_months` tier in the sentence N3 removed and the condition N3 replaced). Closed at both sites. `computations[1].factor_trace[1]` and the `closing_premium_balance` entry of `evaluation_criteria[10].argument_uniqueness_tracing` now give the reason the rule in force actually states — the charges cover six coverage months and leave three of the nine the enrollment has been in force uncovered, which is at least three, so the first tier applies and three coverage months are charged — and both add that each of those months is one the enrollment has already been in force for, so none begins after the coverage end date. The old wording was not merely stale: 'fewer than the nine' is satisfied by a one-month gap, which under the rule in force selects the second tier and one coverage month, so the stated reason did not entail the tier it claimed; and 'the quarter in hand' was the very phrase N3 was closed to remove. No figure moves: the tier taken and the scored 102.80 are unchanged, because 9 less 6 is 3 and 3 meets the real condition.

HOW THE SWEEP CHANGED. Rounds 1 to 3 each left a stale declaration behind because the sweep was keyed on what had been edited: a search for the tokens I had touched cannot find a restatement of the same fact in a different artifact or a different field. This round the sweep is keyed on what a field ASSERTS. Three passes walk every string value at every path of both task files and classify what it claims, ignoring which edit produced it: (1) removed-concept assertions, against a list of every term the charter no longer contains anywhere — ceiling, quarter in hand, card_value_measure, plan_premium_offset, good_cause_excused, settlement_premium_basis, credits_allowed, both months included; (2) figure assertions, where every money-like number in a proof field is checked against the set the world actually produces — every seeded field value, every tier parameter of every product, and every compute binding evaluated at that write's own handling time with the preceding gold writes replayed, plus sums and products of those bindings for stated intermediates; (3) quotation assertions, where every double-quoted fragment of forty characters or more must be found, whitespace- and punctuation-insensitively, in an extended rule, a base rule, a ladder, a tool docstring or the persona. The passes surfaced exactly the sites this round's audit named and no others; the residue they report is historical narrative (figures a superseded form produced, or a rejected reading gives) and counterfactual figures this dossier states on purpose, each of which was checked by replay rather than waved through.

Re-run after these changes: check_extended EXTENDED OK, check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, replay_tasks REPLAY OK, check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK, check_compute COMPUTE OK, check_grounding GROUNDING OK, check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

ROUND 5 — check_traceability, runnable for the first time. The publication of the KB made the traceability gate runnable, and it named a read-ordering defect in task 1, not in this task. I ran the general form of that check over this task as well — for every action, each argument that is an internal row id must appear in the rows some earlier finder call would have returned — and it is clean: the only cross-category read here, find_pdp_premium_ledger at action 6, already follows the find_pdp_enrollments call at action 5 that lands the drug plan's reference number, and every other argument is either a caller-stateable attribute or a reference landed by an earlier read. Nothing in this task changed, and its figures stand at 228.60 and 102.80 with all ten factor baselines and both whole baselines unmoved. Re-run: check_extended EXTENDED OK, check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, replay_tasks REPLAY OK, check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK, check_compute COMPUTE OK, check_grounding GROUNDING OK, check_cross_fire SCOPE OK, check_traceability TRACEABILITY OK.
user_scenario:
Marjorie Calloway is seventy-seven, a retired school librarian in Ridgecrest, and she is telephoning from her own number, 2135550182, on a weekday morning with a cardboard box half packed behind her. Her daughter has found her a place near her own house up in Klamath County and the move happens at the end of this month, so a fortnight ago she posted the plan the form asking to leave the plan she is in, and she has heard nothing back since. What she wants this morning is simply to know the form arrived and is being acted on; she is happy for the representative to look at whatever they need to look at on her record, and if anything has to be done in her own name she will do it herself on the telephone while she has them, provided they tell her plainly what she is agreeing to.

She talks slowly, and she keeps circling back to the same worry, which is that she will arrive in Oregon and find she is somehow still on the books down here. She has no idea how the plan bills her and says so cheerfully; she pays what the paper says when the paper comes.

If the representative asks how to find her she gives her name, and then the number off her red, white and blue Medicare card, 1CW7NQ4RT63, reading it out a letter at a time and repeating it if asked. If they want something further she gives the ZIP code where she lives, 93555. Pressed for her date of birth she will give it, the seventeenth of February 1949, but she offers the card number first because that is the thing sitting in front of her on the table. Nobody else is on the line and she has never appointed anyone to speak for her.

Asked why she is going, she says she is moving to live near her daughter and has already said as much on the form. Asked what she means to do instead, she says she will go back to plain Medicare, and that she understands the prescription cover goes with the plan she is leaving. Asked about money, she says she has been paying the bills as they arrive but cannot remember what she has paid or what is still outstanding, and would rather the representative read it off the record than have her guess; told a figure, she takes it as read and says only that she will watch for the bill.

If the representative says there is something they must put right on her record before they can settle with her, she tells them to go ahead and do whatever the rules call for, and does not ask what it is about. If the representative unlocks a step that only she can take and hands it across to her, she says she is ready and carries it out there and then. Once she is told her plan membership has been brought to an end and what day her coverage runs to, she thanks them warmly, repeats the date back once to be certain she has it, and rings off.

seed_consistency.check: The 2026 Premier enrollment is effectuated on the first day of the month following an election received on 2025-11-19 under the annual election period, which the tier's rule first_of_month_following_receipt carries to 2026-01-01; CMS returned the accepting reply code 011, the identification card was mailed on 2026-01-03, and the status is active with no coverage end date. The tier carries prescription drug coverage, which is why the member's stand-alone drug plan ended the day before this coverage began, as the plan's drug coverage exclusivity rule requires.

The first quarterly charge of 2026 covers the coverage months January to March and is posted on 2026-01-02; at 180.00 it was raised at three times a superseded monthly rate of 60.00 rather than the Premier monthly plan premium of 47.60, which is the over-billing the relief credit addresses.
A part payment of 20.00 by cheque is posted against the oldest unpaid coverage month, 2026-01, leaving part of that charge outstanding, which is what the balance effect partial_payment records.

A second part payment of 20.00 through the online portal is posted a month later, again against the oldest unpaid coverage month 2026-01, and again leaves part of the balance outstanding; its remittance reference differs from the first, so it is not a duplicate posting.

The second quarterly charge covers April to June and is posted on 2026-04-01, the premium due day of that coverage month for this tier, again at the superseded 180.00; it is the most recent plan premium charge standing on the account and so the charge the relief credit names.

A credit adjustment of 60.00 names the single April charge it relieves and carries the reason billing_error_correction; it is less than that charge, so part of it stays outstanding, which the balance effect partial_payment records, and it is the only credit adjustment standing on the account at the opening.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the member profile from the telephone number the caller gives, so the record the whole call runs on is the right one.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile there is no member reference number, and neither the enrollment nor the drug plan record can be reached.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the member whose enrollment is about to be read and changed, on two pieces of information she states herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account may be read out, credited or ended until the in-session verification has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the member's Medicare Advantage enrollment, so the tier held, the billing frequency, the coverage effective date and the current status are on the table.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The monthly plan premium of the tier held, the quarterly billing frequency and the coverage effective date are the inputs every coverage-month count and every premium rate in both computations rests on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every premium ledger entry on the member's Medicare Advantage account: the plan premium charges, the payments posted against them and the credit adjustment already standing there.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan premium reckoned on the account, the coverage months reckoned as owed, the relief already set off, the payments allowed and the relief allowed against the settlement are all aggregates over exactly these rows.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Find the member's own recorded request to leave the plan and read its reference number, request action and intake status.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The enrollment may be brought to an end only on a recorded member request, and that request's reference number is an argument of the member's own action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Look up the Medicare prescription drug plan the member held before this medical plan began and read the low income premium subsidy recorded on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The share of the monthly plan premium the member meets, in both computations, is decided by that recorded subsidy; without it the figures are worked out at the whole monthly plan premium.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read that drug plan's premium account for the low income premium subsidy credits standing on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: How many coverage months the award reaches back over is counted off those credits; without them the award reaches back over none.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the plan's own action for posting a credit to a member's premium account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing on the record and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Put the premium relief the member is owed on her premium account as a single credit entry naming the most recent plan premium charge standing on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The premium relief credited to a member is computed by exactly one policy of this charter, and that figure is the credit amount this action carries.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.advantage_enrollment_id: Value 1c7cd5d4-3e30-4000-9235-e9ba64e89883. Basis: the enrollment record returned at action 2 is the member's only Medicare Advantage enrollment, and the plan premium account being credited is the one the charges stand on; the policy's rule fixes that account as the one where 'the full plan premium stays charged on the account so that what the member owes is always the charge less the credits posted against it'. Uniqueness: no other Medicare Advantage enrollment stands on the profile, and the ended Medicare prescription drug plan is a different product with its own premium account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_premium_entry_id: Value 49c2753b-14fd-4102-8723-1222d2e10c9e. Basis: the rule states that 'The relief owed is posted as a single credit entry naming the most recent plan premium charge standing on the premium account, whatever the size of that charge', which the declared overwrite of the base posting clause makes good. Uniqueness: of the two plan premium charges standing on this account, the one posted 2026-04-01 is later than the one posted 2026-01-02, so the most recent charge is that one and no other; the payment and credit entries on the account are not plan premium charges.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_amount: Value 228.60. The plan premium reckoned on the account is every plan premium charge posted in the contract year, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and two charges stand on it: 180.00 posted 2026-01-02 plus 180.00 posted 2026-04-01, so 360.00. The coverage months reckoned as owed are counted as three for every plan premium charge standing on the account, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and two charges are no more than the nine coverage months it has been in force: 2 times 3 equals 6. The low income premium subsidy award reaches back over three coverage months, because three low income premium subsidy credits stand on the member's Medicare prescription drug plan premium account (17.40 on each of 2025-10-05, 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05). The coverage months chargeable to the member are therefore 6 less 3, that is 3. The share of the monthly plan premium the member meets is half of it, because that drug plan record shows a fifty per cent subsidy, so one coverage month costs 47.60 times 0.5, that is 23.80, and three coverage months cost 71.40. The relief already set off is every credit adjustment posted in the contract year, whatever reason it carries, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and one such entry stands on the account: 60.00 posted 2026-05-11. The relief is 360.00 less 71.40 less 60.00, that is 228.60, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end and not less than nothing.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjustment_reason_code: Value low_income_subsidy_premium_reduction. Basis: the rule states that 'The reason recorded with the credit is the low income premium subsidy the member has been awarded', and the tool's own schema says of that literal that 'the member has been awarded a low income premium subsidy, so the subsidised part of the plan premium is given back'. Uniqueness: not_applicable is only for entries that are not credits; retroactive_rate_change needs a restated plan premium, and no rate restatement stands on the record; duplicate_payment_refund needs the same money twice, and the two payments carry different references; cms_retroactive_disenrollment needs a CMS-directed coverage end, and the enrollment is active with no end date; billing_error_correction is the reason already carried by the credit posted on 2026-05-11; part_b_premium_reduction is handled by Social Security and the base billing rule says the tier's Part B reduction never reaches this account.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the member's own action for ending her plan membership and hand it across to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the member may bring her own enrollment to an end, so the action has to be unlocked and handed over rather than performed by the desk.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The member herself ends her Medicare Advantage enrollment on her own recorded request and the closing plan premium balance is written on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The closing premium balance is computed by exactly one policy of this charter, and it can only be struck once the relief credit stands on the premium account.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.advantage_enrollment_id: Value 1c7cd5d4-3e30-4000-9235-e9ba64e89883. Basis: the intake read at action 4 records the request against this enrollment, and the enrollment record returned at action 2 shows it as the member's active Medicare Advantage coverage. Uniqueness: it is the only Medicare Advantage enrollment on the profile, and the drug plan record returned at action 5 already carries the status disenrolled with a coverage end date of 2025-12-31, so there is nothing there to end.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.advantage_enrollment_request_id: Value 2d83c46f-1cd5-4a38-9532-23a57d50b88c. Basis: the base rule that 'A request to end the enrollment is recorded on the enrollment intake with the request action voluntary_disenrollment and an intake status of recorded, awaiting_member_signature or submitted_to_cms before the enrollment is ended' pins the action to that recorded request; the intake read at action 4 carries the request action voluntary_disenrollment and the intake status recorded. Uniqueness: it is the only enrollment intake on the profile, and the customer states she 'posted the plan the form asking to leave the plan she is in', which is that request.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.closing_premium_balance: Value 102.80. The plan premium reckoned against the settlement is every plan premium charge posted in the contract year, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and two charges stand on it: 360.00. The coverage months the settlement still charges for are three, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and the charges standing on the account cover six coverage months, leaving three of the nine the enrollment has been in force uncovered, which is at least three; each of those three is a coverage month already in force, so none of them begins after the coverage end date. A coverage month the settlement charges for is priced at the monthly plan premium of the tier held taken at the share charged to the member, which is half of it because the drug plan record shows a fifty per cent subsidy: 47.60 times 0.5 is 23.80, and three coverage months come to 71.40. The payments allowed against the settlement are every plan premium payment posted in the contract year, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and two payments stand on the account: 20.00 posted 2026-01-09 plus 20.00 posted 2026-02-10, that is 40.00. The relief allowed against the settlement is every credit adjustment posted in the contract year, whatever reason each carries, because the enrollment is billed quarterly and, once the relief credit of 228.60 has been posted, two such entries stand on the account: 60.00 plus 228.60, that is 288.60. The closing balance is 360.00 plus 71.40 less 40.00 less 288.60, that is 102.80, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end and not less than nothing.

edges.condition: A credit entry for the premium relief the member is owed stands on the premium account of the enrollment being ended.
edges.policy_source: The closing premium balance is not struck before the premium relief the member is owed stands on the premium account as a credit entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At the opening the only credit entry on this premium account is the 60.00 billing error correction posted on 2026-05-11 against the April charge. The premium relief the member is owed under the low income premium subsidy recorded on her drug plan record is 228.60 and no entry for it stands anywhere on the account: the two plan premium charges total 360.00, the only credit against them is that 60.00, and the subsidy award that reduces what she is liable for has left no trace on this account at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Posting the relief credit of 228.60 against the 2026-04-01 charge puts a second credit adjustment on the account, so the relief allowed against the settlement moves from 0.00 (one credit adjustment standing, none of it posted within the last three months) to 288.60 (two credit adjustments standing on a quarterly-billed account, so every credit adjustment of the contract year is allowed), and the closing premium balance falls from 391.40 to 102.80.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain with one edge, so there is only one topological order: the relief credit is posted, then the closing balance is struck. No two writes of this task are free to be reordered, and the dependent write reads the very rows the depended-on write adds, so the order is entailed rather than chosen. It is entailed a second time by base: advantage_premium_posting allows a credit adjustment only while the enrollment is active, premium_grace_period or terminated_for_nonpayment, and the member's own write leaves it disenrolled.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the relief credit and replaying everything else leaves one credit adjustment standing on the premium account and none of it inside the last three months, so the relief allowed against the settlement is 0.00 instead of 288.60 and the closing premium balance comes out at 391.40 instead of 102.80.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario nowhere mentions a credit, a subsidy, an overcharge or anything else that has to be put right on the premium account, and it names no second piece of work. The customer says only that she posted a form asking to leave the plan, that she wants to know it arrived, that she will go back to plain Medicare, and that she cannot remember what she has paid. Her only contribution touching the prerequisite is passive and conditional: if the representative tells her there is something they must put right on her record first, she says to go ahead. She never asks whether anything has to be sorted out first and never mentions a figure being wrong.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: end_plan_membership_007ca425 does not read the premium ledger at all: its body computes the coverage end date from the handling clock and issues two ctx.update calls, one writing status, coverage end date, disenrollment reason and the closing balance on the enrollment, one marking the intake carried out. It never checks whether a relief credit stands on the account, never refuses, never errors and returns the same confirmation whatever the ledger holds. Calling it before the credit is posted writes a closing balance of 391.40 and the difference shows up only in the terminal hash.
